items.stem: Define the term 'market share'.
items.answer: The sales of one business as a percentage of the total sales of the market in a period.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The sales of one business as a percentage of the total sales of the market in a period. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why it is useful to use more than one measure of business size.
items.answer: Each measure can mislead: a capital-intensive business may have few employees and a retailer may have high revenue but low capital employed, so using several measures gives a fairer picture.
items.markingKey: 1 mark measures can mislead; 1 mark example; 1 mark combined picture. [3]

items.stem: Explain why profit is not usually used as a measure of business size.
items.answer: Profit depends on efficiency, prices and the state of the economy; a large business may make a loss and a small one a high profit in some years.
items.markingKey: 1 mark profit reflects performance not size; 1 mark example/variability. [2]

items.stem: Labour turnover among machinists has risen sharply this year. Tanvir Textiles Ltd, a private limited company in Bangladesh with about 420 employees, makes shirts and T-shirts for European fashion retailers. Explain why Tanvir Textiles might appear large on one measure of size but small on another.
items.answer: Points to develop for Tanvir Textiles: different measures capture different aspects of size; capital intensity affects employee numbers; prices affect revenue; market size affects market share.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: different measures capture different aspects of size. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Tanvir Textiles (clothing manufacturing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. capital intensity affects employee numbers; prices affect revenue. [3]

items.stem: A global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours. Nusantara Apparel Tbk, a public limited company in Indonesia with about 4,000 employees, makes sportswear under contract for global brands. Explain why Nusantara Apparel might appear large on one measure of size but small on another.
items.answer: Points to develop for Nusantara Apparel: different measures capture different aspects of size; capital intensity affects employee numbers; prices affect revenue; market size affects market share.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: different measures capture different aspects of size. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Nusantara Apparel (clothing manufacturing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. capital intensity affects employee numbers; prices affect revenue. [3]

items.stem: Based in Alexandria, Atlas Furniture plc (public limited company) makes furniture and sells it through 40 stores. The business has around 1,300 employees. Sales in its stores have fallen while online sales have grown. Evaluate the most appropriate way to measure the size of Atlas Furniture.
items.answer: For: market share shows position in the market; revenue shows scale of sales; capital employed shows investment. Against: each measure can mislead; comparisons across industries are difficult; data may not be available for rivals. Judgement: for Atlas Furniture it depends mainly on the purpose of the comparison, and also on the industry.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Atlas Furniture: furniture manufacturing and retail, about 1,300 employees, public limited company in Egypt; sales in its stores have fallen while online sales have grown). AO3 Analysis [3]: arguments for, e.g. market share shows position in the market; revenue shows scale of sales; capital employed shows investment; arguments against, e.g. each measure can mislead; comparisons across industries are difficult; data may not be available for rivals. AO4 Evaluation [3]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the purpose of the comparison; the industry; the data available. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Atlas Furniture. [10]

items.stem: Why might the number of employees be a misleading measure of the size of a business?
options: All businesses have the same number of employees
Capital-intensive businesses may have large output with few employees
Employees cannot be counted
It is the same as market share
items.answer: Capital-intensive businesses may have large output with few employees
items.markingKey: Capital-intensive businesses may have large output with few employees. Highly automated firms employ few workers but may be very large. [1]

items.stem: Kaya Cycles is a partnership based in Mombasa, Kenya. It sells and repairs bicycles and motorbikes and employs about 9 people. The two partners disagree about whether to borrow money to expand. Identify and explain one advantage for Kaya Cycles of using revenue to compare its size with competitors.
items.answer: Easy to obtain and understand; this would help Kaya Cycles, which sells and repairs bicycles and motorbikes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. easy to obtain and understand; shows the scale of sales; useful within the same industry. 1 mark: explained in the context of Kaya Cycles (retail and repairs). [2]

items.stem: Define the term 'small business'.
items.answer: A business with few employees and low revenue and capital compared with others in its industry, often owned and run by the same people.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – A business with few employees and low revenue and capital compared with others in its industry, often owned and run by the same people. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain two reasons why small businesses are important to an economy.
items.answer: They create many jobs, especially in local communities; and they increase competition, which keeps prices down and encourages innovation, and some grow into large businesses.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark point, 1 mark explanation): jobs, competition, innovation, supply large firms, future large firms. [4]

items.stem: Explain why small businesses can survive in markets dominated by large businesses.
items.answer: They can serve niche markets, offer personal and flexible service, and supply specialist products that large firms find unprofitable.
items.markingKey: 1 mark niche; 1 mark personal service/flexibility; 1 mark local knowledge. [3]

items.stem: Most customers book in the dry season and cash is short in the wet season. Blue Lagoon Tours, a partnership in Fiji with about 14 employees, runs boat trips and diving courses for tourists. Explain the problems that Blue Lagoon Tours may face because of its size.
items.answer: Points to develop for Blue Lagoon Tours: small businesses have limited resources; difficulty raising finance; higher unit costs; dependence on a few customers or the owner.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: small businesses have limited resources. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Blue Lagoon Tours (tourism). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. difficulty raising finance; higher unit costs. [3]

items.stem: Based in Alexandria, Atlas Furniture plc (public limited company) makes furniture and sells it through 40 stores. The business has around 1,300 employees. Sales in its stores have fallen while online sales have grown. Explain how Atlas Furniture could compete with much larger rivals.
items.answer: Points to develop for Atlas Furniture: small firms lack economies of scale; focus on a niche such as smart office furniture; personal service and flexibility; local knowledge and reputation.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: small firms lack economies of scale. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Atlas Furniture (furniture manufacturing and retail). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. focus on a niche such as smart office furniture; personal service and flexibility. [3]

items.stem: Tanvir Textiles is a private limited company in Dhaka, Bangladesh with about 420 staff. It makes shirts and T-shirts for European fashion retailers. Labour turnover among machinists has risen sharply this year. Evaluate whether small businesses such as Tanvir Textiles have a future in an economy dominated by large firms.
items.answer: For: niche markets; flexibility and personal service; government support. Against: large firms have lower costs; online giants reach every market; finance is hard to obtain. Judgement: for Tanvir Textiles it depends mainly on the type of market, and also on how far customers value personal service.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Tanvir Textiles: clothing manufacturing, about 420 employees, private limited company in Bangladesh; labour turnover among machinists has risen sharply this year). AO3 Analysis [3]: arguments for, e.g. niche markets; flexibility and personal service; government support; arguments against, e.g. large firms have lower costs; online giants reach every market; finance is hard to obtain. AO4 Evaluation [3]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the type of market; how far customers value personal service; government policy. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Tanvir Textiles. [10]

items.stem: Kiwi Trails Ltd is a private limited company based in Auckland, New Zealand. It runs guided hiking, kayaking and cycling tours and employs about 90 people. Bookings are highly seasonal and most guides are employed only for the summer. Explain one disadvantage to Kiwi Trails of remaining a small business.
items.answer: Higher average costs; this would be a problem for Kiwi Trails, which runs guided hiking, kayaking and cycling tours.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. higher average costs; harder to raise finance; vulnerable if a large competitor enters. 1 mark: explained in the context of Kiwi Trails (tourism). [2]

items.stem: Its car-maker customers are switching rapidly to electric vehicles. Deccan Auto Components Ltd, a public limited company in India with about 2,200 employees, supplies brakes and steering parts to car manufacturers. Explain the problems that Deccan Auto may face because of its size.
items.answer: Points to develop for Deccan Auto: small businesses have limited resources; difficulty raising finance; higher unit costs; dependence on a few customers or the owner.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: small businesses have limited resources. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Deccan Auto (automotive components). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. difficulty raising finance; higher unit costs. [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'internal (organic) growth'.
items.answer: Expansion of a business by increasing its own output and sales, for example by opening new outlets or launching new products.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Expansion of a business by increasing its own output and sales, for example by opening new outlets or launching new products. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain two economies of scale that a growing business might benefit from.
items.answer: Purchasing economies: buying in bulk lowers the cost per unit; financial economies: larger firms can borrow more cheaply because banks see them as less risky.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark economy, 1 mark explanation): purchasing, technical, financial, marketing, managerial. [4]

items.stem: Explain why internal growth is often slower but less risky than external growth.
items.answer: Internal growth happens gradually using the firm's own resources, so managers keep control and the culture is preserved; external growth is fast but involves integrating another business, which often fails.
items.markingKey: 1 mark internal gradual; 1 mark lower risk/control; 1 mark external integration risks. [3]

items.stem: Based in Amman, Petra Prints Ltd (private limited company) prints leaflets, posters and packaging for local businesses. The business has around 35 employees. A large customer has started to pay its invoices late. Explain the benefits to Petra Prints of growing internally rather than externally.
items.answer: Points to develop for Petra Prints: internal growth expands the business from within; lower risk and less finance needed at once; managers keep control and the culture is preserved; growth may be too slow if rivals expand quickly.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: internal growth expands the business from within. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Petra Prints (printing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. lower risk and less finance needed at once; managers keep control and the culture is preserved. [3]

items.stem: Based in Guadalajara, Rosa Bakes (sole trader) bakes bread and cakes in a small shop and supplies three local cafés. The business has around 6 employees. The owner, Rosa, is thinking of opening a second shop. Explain how economies of scale could benefit Rosa Bakes if it doubles its output of bread and cakes.
items.answer: Points to develop for Rosa Bakes: economies of scale lower average costs; purchasing economies from bulk buying; technical economies from larger machinery; lower costs allow lower prices or higher margins.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: economies of scale lower average costs. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Rosa Bakes (food retail). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. purchasing economies from bulk buying; technical economies from larger machinery. [3]

items.stem: Sunrise Juices is a private limited company in Kingston, Jamaica with about 60 staff. It makes fresh fruit juices sold to supermarkets and hotels. A new supermarket chain wants to stock its juices if it can supply larger quantities. Explain the benefits to Sunrise Juices of growing internally rather than externally.
items.answer: Points to develop for Sunrise Juices: internal growth expands the business from within; lower risk and less finance needed at once; managers keep control and the culture is preserved; growth may be too slow if rivals expand quickly.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: internal growth expands the business from within. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Sunrise Juices (food and drink manufacturing). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. lower risk and less finance needed at once; managers keep control and the culture is preserved. [4]

items.stem: Based in Bangkok, Siam Ready Meals Co. Ltd (private limited company) produces chilled and frozen ready meals for supermarkets and convenience stores. The business has around 1,100 employees. Its biggest customer, a convenience-store chain, wants deliveries twice a day. Evaluate whether Siam Ready Meals should grow internally or externally.
items.answer: For: internal: lower risk and control; external: fast growth and new markets; external gives immediate economies of scale. Against: internal is slow; external may face integration problems and culture clashes; both need finance. Judgement: for Siam Ready Meals it depends mainly on how fast its market is changing, and also on the finance available.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Siam Ready Meals: food manufacturing, about 1,100 employees, private limited company in Thailand; its biggest customer, a convenience-store chain, wants deliveries twice a day). AO3 Analysis [3]: arguments for, e.g. internal: lower risk and control; external: fast growth and new markets; external gives immediate economies of scale; arguments against, e.g. internal is slow; external may face integration problems and culture clashes; both need finance. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Siam Ready Meals. [10]

items.stem: Maple Learning Inc. is a private limited company based in Toronto, Canada. It runs an online tutoring and test-preparation platform for school students and employs about 260 people. Venture capital investors expect it to become profitable within two years. Discuss whether growth always benefits a business such as Maple Learning.
items.answer: For: economies of scale; more market power; security from takeover. Against: diseconomies of scale; loss of flexibility; financial risk from borrowing to grow. Judgement: for Maple Learning it depends mainly on how growth is managed, and also on the market conditions.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Maple Learning: education technology, about 260 employees, private limited company in Canada; venture capital investors expect it to become profitable within two years). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. economies of scale; more market power; security from takeover; arguments against, e.g. diseconomies of scale; loss of flexibility; financial risk from borrowing to grow. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on how growth is managed; the market conditions; the objectives of the owners. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Maple Learning. [12]

items.stem: Which is an example of internal growth?
options: Merging with a supplier
Taking over a rival business
Opening ten new branches funded from retained profit
Buying shares in a competitor to gain control
items.answer: Opening ten new branches funded from retained profit
items.markingKey: Opening ten new branches funded from retained profit. Organic growth uses the business's own expansion. [1]

Explain one disadvantage to BatikPay of growing much larger.
items.answer: Diseconomies of scale, which matters for BatikPay because it runs a mobile payments app used by 4 million customers and 90 000 small shops.
items.markingKey: 1 mark knowledge: a relevant disadvantage, e.g. diseconomies of scale; loss of personal contact with customers; greater need for finance. 1 mark application to BatikPay (financial technology). 1 mark analysis: consequence for the business developed. [3]

items.answer: Points to develop for Lanka Tea: internal growth expands the business from within; lower risk and less finance needed at once; managers keep control and the culture is preserved; growth may be too slow if rivals expand quickly.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: internal growth expands the business from within. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Lanka Tea (agriculture and food). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. lower risk and less finance needed at once; managers keep control and the culture is preserved. [3]

items.stem: Mosaic Apps Ltd is a private limited company based in Casablanca, Morocco. It develops booking apps for restaurants and hairdressers and employs about 28 people. items.answer: (a) Expansion of a business by merging with or taking over other businesses. (b) Internal growth expands the business from within; lower risk and less finance needed at once; managers keep control and the culture is preserved; growth may be too slow if rivals expand quickly.

items.stem: Define the term 'merger'.
items.answer: An agreement by the owners of two businesses to join together to form one business.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – An agreement by the owners of two businesses to join together to form one business. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain one reason why many mergers and takeovers fail to achieve their objectives.
items.answer: Different business cultures clash and integrating the two businesses' systems and staff is harder and more costly than expected, so the planned cost savings do not happen.
items.markingKey: 1 mark reason (culture clash/integration problems/overpaying); 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.stem: Explain two benefits of horizontal integration.
items.answer: Economies of scale from combined production and purchasing; and higher market share, which reduces competition and gives more control over prices.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark point, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Based in Mumbai, Deccan Auto Components Ltd (public limited company) supplies brakes and steering parts to car manufacturers. The business has around 2,200 employees. Its car-maker customers are switching rapidly to electric vehicles. Explain why Deccan Auto might choose conglomerate integration.
items.answer: Points to develop for Deccan Auto: conglomerate integration joins unrelated businesses; spreads risk across markets; uses spare finance or management skills; managers may lack knowledge of the new industry.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: conglomerate integration joins unrelated businesses. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Deccan Auto (automotive components). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. spreads risk across markets; uses spare finance or management skills. [3]

items.stem: Lotus Spa is a sole trader in Chiang Mai, Thailand with about 8 staff. It offers massages and beauty treatments. The owner wants to introduce online booking and loyalty discounts. Explain the possible benefits to Lotus Spa of a takeover of one of its suppliers.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lotus Spa: backward vertical integration joins with a supplier; secure supply of inputs for spa treatments; better control of quality and delivery times; lower costs as the supplier's margin is absorbed.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: backward vertical integration joins with a supplier. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Lotus Spa (personal services). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. secure supply of inputs for spa treatments; better control of quality and delivery times. [3]

items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: a merger combines two businesses. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Andean Coffee (food processing). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. culture clashes between staff; integration of systems is costly. [4]
